clue.text: Uppity tramp, devout, hogging entrance to temple

parts.note: a bum is a vagrant or tramp

indicators.note: something hogging another thing holds it greedily, so the word for devout takes a letter inside

parts.note: devout means pious

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter, here the start of temple

explanation.surface: A scruffy vagrant who is also churchy, blocking the temple doorway, seems uppity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bumptious is self-important and pushy, much as an uppity person gets above their station.

clue.text: Two-timer — big-time — taking in foreign friends

indicators.note: the pieces from big-time take another piece inside, as a house takes in a lodger

parts.note: taken as written
amis is French for friends

explanation.surface: A big-time two-timer welcomes friends from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigamist is married to two people at once, the ultimate case of two-timing a partner.

clue.text: Idiot and person of faith losing marbles, initially

indicators.note: losing says a letter drops out of the believer's name

parts.note: a Mormon is a member of the Latter-day Saints church

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of marbles

explanation.surface: A fool and a believer who have both lost their marbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing marbles' reads as going mad, but only the M at the start of marbles is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Moron is a common insult synonym for an idiot or very stupid person.

clue.text: "Doth Hosea have thy date off?" — well dodgy Biblical location

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the quoted words and well are to be rearranged

parts.words: Doth Hosea have thy date off

explanation.surface: A garbled question about the prophet Hosea's dates is dismissed as rather dubious scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: All 27 letters of the quotation plus WELL are rearranged; 'dodgy' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from Psalm 23, a place of danger the psalmist walks through without fear.

clue.text: See 3
Soothes twisted tongue

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters of soothes are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something soothes a tongue that has been twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesotho is a Bantu language of Lesotho and South Africa; tongue means a language.

clue.text: Go mad backwards

indicators.note: backwards tells you to read the word for mad from end to start

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: An instruction to go crazy in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go at something is to have a stab at it, so the two nouns mean an attempt.

clue.text: Eatery offering up tune with egregious skill

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole string is read from the bottom, so the three pieces run backwards

parts.note: an air is a melody
OTT, over the top, means outrageous or egregious
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A restaurant serves up a song performed with outrageous flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the whole run AIROTTART, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian restaurant, a kind of eatery.

clue.text: Drink manufacturer's little brown jug

parts.note: br is a short form of brown
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: A drinks maker sells a small brown jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewer makes beer, a drink produced by brewing.

clue.text: Onset of sudden infatuation involving frottage with bishop's cleaning equipment

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its opening letter, here of sudden
involving means enclosing, so the word for infatuation wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: a crush is a passing infatuation
frottage is rubbing, in art or otherwise
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A sudden racy passion with a bishop ends up as a lesson in cleaning kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Frottage is rubbing, here put to a clean use.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrubbing brush is a stiff-bristled brush used to scour floors and surfaces clean.

clue.text: Surfeit of blood and guts originally included

indicators.note: included says that first letter is put inside the word for blood

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of guts

explanation.surface: A horror film offers too much blood and guts.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorge is an excessive meal, so the noun names a surfeit of food.

clue.text: Dubious sources of early English texts, sacred and profane

indicators.note: dubious means doubtful or suspect, so the letters are put in a new order
the sources of the three words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Questionable origins of old English writings, both holy and irreverent.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials E, E, T join SACRED and all nine letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To profane something holy is to treat it with irreverence, as a verb meaning to violate it.

clue.text: Statesman swapping energy for a mystic symbol

indicators.note: swapping one thing for another says a letter in the name is replaced

parts.note: Nelson Mandela was the South African statesman
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A politician trades in his energy for something mystical.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandala is a circular design representing the universe in Hindu and Buddhist practice.

clue.text: Set out to be 22d by faithful steward

indicators.note: 22 across is a word meaning hug, so to be hugged by means to sit inside another word

parts.note: true means loyal or faithful

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loyal steward is set out to be hugged.
explanation.walkthrough: 22d reads as 22 + d: the answer to 22 across with a D added, i.e. embraced. STE (set out) sits inside TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trustee holds and manages property for others, a kind of steward.

clue.text: Hat and belt converted into shady American bit of military hardware

indicators.note: into says the rearranged letters go inside the next word

parts.note: somber, the American spelling of sombre, means dark or shady

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters of hat and belt are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hat and belt are turned into a shadowy US warplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' also tells you to use the US spelling SOMBER, not SOMBRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The stealth bomber is a US aircraft designed to evade radar, a piece of military kit.

clue.text: Delight composer, backing virgin keeping quiet, finally

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the composer's name is reversed

parts.note: Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia

indicators.note: keeping says the word for virgin holds a letter inside

parts.note: pure means chaste or virgin

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of quiet

explanation.surface: A composer is thrilled by backing a virgin who keeps quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrapture someone is to fill them with delight, both verbs meaning to thrill.

clue.text: Little man's insides corrupted by sloth?

indicators.note: in, split off the front of insides, says the rearranged letters go inside
corrupted means spoilt or altered, so the letters of sides are rearranged

parts.note: Len is a short form of Leonard, a little version of a man's name

explanation.surface: A small man's guts have rotted through laziness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insides' splits as IN + SIDES: IDESS (from SIDES) wraps round LEN. The question mark flags sloth as the sin, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is laziness, one of the seven deadly sins, and idleness is a synonym for it.

clue.text: Par for Windsor flag?

parts.note: par means standard, and Windsor is the royal family's name, so the standard of the Windsors is the royal one

explanation.surface: A golf score for a flag over Windsor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Standard is the British monarch's flag, flown over Windsor Castle when the sovereign is there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Standard is the personal banner of the British sovereign.

clue.text: Teletubby introducing student to Poles' dialect

indicators.note: introducing means bringing in, so the Teletubby's name takes a letter inside

parts.note: Laa-Laa is the yellow Teletubby of the children's TV show, here spelt Lala
L, for learner, stands for a student
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A children's TV character brings a student to meet some Polish speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lallans is the Lowland Scots dialect, used in literature by Burns and others.

clue.text: Head lice possibly infesting cyclist's accoutrement

indicators.note: infesting means swarming inside, so the rearranged letters go into the word for head

parts.note: the top of something is its head

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of lice may be in some other order

explanation.surface: Head lice might be found on a cyclist's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A toe clip is a cage on a bicycle pedal holding the rider's foot in place.

clue.text: See 3
Huge flop — catastrophic — no good looking on the bright side

indicators.note: catastrophic means disastrous, so the letters of huge flop are shuffled
no says the following letter is left out

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of huge flop

explanation.surface: After a disastrous failure, someone still stays optimistic.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop G from the letters of HUGE FLOP and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopeful describes someone optimistic, expecting things to turn out well.

clue.text: Shed returning couple's gesture of affection

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for the setter is reversed

parts.note: Shed is the setter, so the setter refers to himself as me
a brace is a pair or couple, as of pheasants

explanation.surface: A garden shed goes back to a couple for a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed is the setter's pseudonym, standing for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrace is a hug, an act showing affection.

clue.text: Lofty peaks in African desert

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: High mountains rising out of an African desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the long South American mountain chain with some very high peaks.

clue.text: Talking dog left eating hard black dumpling

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the dog and L enclose the next letters

parts.note: Dougal is the talking dog in the children's TV show The Magic Roundabout
H stands for hard, as in pencil grades
B stands for black, as in pencil grades

explanation.surface: A talking dog is left chewing a hard black dumpling.
explanation.walkthrough: HB is the pencil grade 'hard black'. DOUGAL is from The Magic Roundabout, a British children's TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: A dough ball is a small round dumpling made of dough.

clue.text: A Parisian twosome, almost de trop

parts.note: un is French for a, as said in Paris

indicators.note: almost says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a duet is a performance by two

explanation.surface: A French couple seem a bit too much.
explanation.definitionFit: De trop means excessive or unwelcome, the same as undue, which means more than is warranted.

clue.text: Wherewithal to get stoned or pissed?

definitions.meaning: cannabis is the means of getting high
here meaning having urinated, written as a contracted past tense

explanation.surface: What does it take to get high or drunk?
explanation.walkthrough: 'pissed' looks like British slang for drunk, but it means urinated: WEE'D.
explanation.definitionFit: Weed is slang for cannabis, and wee'd is the past of wee, to urinate.

clue.text: Old dykes from which ship's past can be reconstructed

indicators.note: can be reconstructed says the letters can be built again in another order

explanation.surface: Ancient dykes from which a ship's history can be pieced together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dykes' looks like sea walls, from which a ship's past might be read; the 's of ship's is a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphists, after the poet Sappho, is an old term for lesbians; dyke is slang for the same.
